author: Athanasius of Alexandria
occasion: Athanasius writes to the presbyter Palladius after receiving a letter from him, and after learning through Innocentius and Dianius that monks in Caesarea are grieved and resisting Bishop Basil. He writes to commend Palladius's orthodoxy and to urge that the monks be persuaded to accept Basil.
argument: Athanasius rejoices at Palladius's letter and his customary orthodoxy, and approves the cause he shares with Innocentius. He has learned that the monks in Caesarea are grieved and resisting Bishop Basil, but he has written to them what is fitting: they should obey Basil as children obey a father. Since Basil is a boast of the Church, contending for the truth and teaching those in need, the monks appear to be grieved in vain. Athanasius asks Palladius to make this known to them, so that they may be persuaded, show themselves to be well-disposed toward their father, and preserve peace in the Churches.

outline.move: Athanasius greets Palladius, praises his orthodoxy, addresses the Caesarean monks' opposition to Basil, and asks Palladius to persuade them to accept Basil for the sake of truth and peace.

cast.name: Athanasius
cast.who: Bishop of Alexandria and author of the letter.

cast.name: Palladius
cast.who: A presbyter and the letter's addressee.

cast.name: Innocentius
cast.who: A beloved associate with whom Palladius is engaged in a cause.

cast.name: Dianius
cast.who: A beloved associate from whom Athanasius learned that the Caesarean monks were grieved and resisting Basil.

cast.name: Basil
cast.who: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, opposed by some monks but described by Athanasius as a boast of the Church.

voices.speaker: Athanasius
voices.how_marked: The entire letter is presented as Athanasius's own first-person address.

key_terms.sense: Right belief or orthodox faith, which Palladius is said to breathe.
Monks, specifically those in Caesarea who are distressed and opposing Basil.
The truth of Christian faith, for which Basil contends and about which suspicion would justify opposition.
A boast or source of pride for the Church, applied to Basil.
Basil's pastoral accommodation or management, by which he becomes weak to the weak.
Bishop, the office held by Basil and Athanasius.
Peace among the churches, which Athanasius wants preserved by the monks' acceptance of Basil.

scripture: The letter contains no explicit biblical citations, but it alludes to 1 Corinthians 9:22 ('to the weak I became weak, that I might gain the weak'). If cited, use modern forms such as 1 Corinthians.
uncertain: The exact date of the letter.
The precise nature of the cause Palladius shares with Innocentius.
The specific reasons for the Caesarean monks' opposition to Basil beyond what Athanasius reports.

_unresolved_facts.claim: after learning through Innocentius and Dianius that monks in Caesarea are grieved and resisting Bishop Basil
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τὴν αἰτίαν δὲ ἣν μετὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Ἰνοκεντίου διάγεις, οὐ πρῶτον νῦν, ἀλλ' ἔκπαλαι μαθὼν, ἀπεδεξάμην σου τὴν εὐλάβειαν... ἔμαθον δὲ παρὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Διανίου, ὡς λυπουμένων καὶ ἀνθισταμένων αὐτῶν τῷ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Βασιλείῳ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Athanasius had long known of the cause Palladius shares with Innocentius; he learned specifically about the monks' grief and resistance to Basil through Dianius alone, not through both Innocentius and Dianius.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He writes to commend Palladius's orthodoxy and to urge that the monks be persuaded to accept Basil
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: σὲ μὲν ἀπεδεξάμην δηλώσαντα, αὐτοῖς δὲ τὰ πρέποντα δεδήλωκα... Καὶ σὺ οὖν, ἀγαπητὲ, θέλησον αὐτοῖς δηλῶσαι, ἵνα, ὡς ἔγραψα, πεισθῶσι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Athanasius has already written to the monks himself (δεδήλωκα), and now asks Palladius to make his own prior communication known to them (δηλῶσαι), not to persuade them himself.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He has learned that the monks in Caesarea are grieved and resisting Bishop Basil, but he has written to them what is fitting
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἔμαθον δὲ παρὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Διανίου, ὡς λυπουμένων καὶ ἀνθισταμένων αὐτῶν... αὐτοῖς δὲ τὰ πρέποντα δεδήλωκα
_unresolved_facts.fix: Athanasius learned from Dianius that the monks were grieved and resisting; he had already written to them (perfect tense δεδήλωκα indicates completed action with present relevance), not that he writes now in response.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Athanasius asks Palladius to make this known to them, so that they may be persuaded
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Καὶ σὺ οὖν, ἀγαπητὲ, θέλησον αὐτοῖς δηλῶσαι, ἵνα, ὡς ἔγραψα, πεισθῶσι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Athanasius asks Palladius to make known to them what Athanasius himself has already written (ὡς ἔγραψα), so that they may be persuaded by Athanasius's prior letter.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Innocentius... A beloved associate with whom Palladius is engaged in a cause
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τὴν αἰτίαν δὲ ἣν μετὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Ἰνοκεντίου διάγεις
_unresolved_facts.fix: Innocentius is a beloved associate with whom Palladius pursues a cause (αἰτία), but 'cause' here may imply a legal case, dispute, or shared purpose rather than general engagement; the term διάγεις suggests Palladius is conducting or managing this cause with Innocentius.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Dianius... A beloved associate from whom Athanasius learned that the Caesarean monks were grieved and resisting Basil
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐξ ὧν γὰρ διηγήσατο ὁ ἀγαπητὸς Διάνιος
_unresolved_facts.fix: Dianius is described as having narrated or reported (διηγήσατο) details to Athanasius, which goes beyond simply learning facts—he gave an account that included Basil's approach to the weak (τοῖς ἀσθενοῦσιν ἀσθενὴς γίνεται).
